record.context_brief: Finite-dimensional closure of two additive one-parameter subgroups
record.original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let k[x1, ..., xn] be the polynomial algebra, and let P and Q be locally nilpotent derivations of k[x1, ..., xn]. Consider the two one-parameter subgroups {exp(tP) | t in k} and {exp(tQ) | t in k} of Aut_k(k[x1, ..., xn]). Under what conditions is the minimal closed subgroup of Aut_k(k[x1, ..., xn]) that contains both of these one-parameter subgroups finite-dimensional?

evidence.quote: 3. Two Locally Nilpotent Derivations Let P and Q be locally nilpotent derivations of k[n].
Problem 3.1. When is the minimal closed subgroup of Aut_k k[n] containing the one-dimensional subgroups {exp tP | t in k} and {exp tQ | t in k} finite dimensional?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and let $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ denote the polynomial algebra in $n$ variables over $k$. A $k$-linear derivation $D$ of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is called locally nilpotent if for every $f \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ there exists a positive integer $m$ (depending on $f$) such that $D^m(f) = 0$. For any locally nilpotent derivation $D$, the formal exponential
$$\exp(tD) = \sum_{m\ge 0} \frac{t^m D^m}{m!}$$
defines, for each $t \in k$, an automorphism of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, and $\{\exp(tD) \mid t \in k\}$ is a one-parameter subgroup of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}_k(k[x_1,\dots,x_n])$, which carries its natural ind-group structure (so that "closed subgroup" and "finite-dimensional subgroup" are well-defined notions).

Let $P$ and $Q$ be two locally nilpotent derivations of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, and let $G(P,Q)$ denote the minimal closed subgroup of $\mathrm{Aut}_k(k[x_1,\dots,x_n])$ containing the two one-parameter subgroups $\{\exp(tP) \mid t \in k\}$ and $\{\exp(tQ) \mid t \in k\}$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(P,Q)$ under which $G(P,Q)$ is finite-dimensional.
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive resolution of this question regarding when the closed subgroup of polynomial automorphisms generated by two additive one-parameter subgroups arising from locally nilpotent derivations is finite-dimensional was located. The problem appears to remain open in general, with only partial results known in low dimensions and for commuting derivations, but the search did not produce conclusive evidence.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem on when the minimal closed subgroup containing two exp(tP), exp(tQ) is finite-dimensional is posed.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as an open problem with no resolution indicated.
